Subject: NimbleHealth — integration recap & next steps (SDK, VPC endpoint, reranker)

Hi Samir / Priya,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through the classification + triage flows. Below is a concise recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the Proof-of-Concept (PoC).

Call recap (high level)
- Goal: route clinical notes into a fast, private inference path for classification + reranking, then surface structured output to downstream triage systems.
- Data sensitivity: some PII/PHI in scope — NimbleHealth prefers a private connectivity option (VPC endpoint / PrivateLink) and mTLS where possible.
- Key features we discussed: SDK-based request routing, structured output/tool-calling for rerankers, embeddings for semantic matching, and stable egress/IP allowlisting for firewalling.

Immediate asks / owners
1) SDK onboarding: Jonas will send an onboarding checklist and a minimal SDK init example to test against the sandbox endpoint (action: jonas_weber) — attached checklist.
2) Auth model: confirm whether NimbleHealth wants API-key + TLS for sandbox vs. mTLS for production private endpoint (action: nimble).
3) Private connectivity: Ben to propose VPC endpoint pattern and egress model (action: ben_carter).
4) Reranker/embeddings: recommended approach is to run embeddings in the same private deployment and call a lightweight reranker via structured outputs for top-K scoring (action: product/eng alignment).

Proposed next steps
- Ben and I will follow up with a short technical note on: (a) IP allowlist ranges per region, (b) PrivateLink vs VPC peering tradeoffs, and (c) how Redwood handles cert rotation for mTLS.
- Suggest 30–45 minute tech deep-dive next week (tentative: Thu 1pm PT) to agree on the network pattern and initial pilot scope.

Attachments: redwood-onramp-checklist.xlsx; demo-recording-nimble.mp4 (link)

Samir / Priya —

Quick technical answers and a short checklist to unblock decisions before Thursday:

1) mTLS cert rotation\- model: Redwood supports two patterns for private deployments:
   a) Customer-managed certs: Nimble supplies a CA and short-lived client certs (recommended when you require full custody). Redwood will validate client certs presented during the TLS handshake.
   b) Redwood-managed rotation: we can manage cert issuance and rotation on your behalf if you prefer. In that case, Redwood stores and rotates keys in your KMS (recommended for lower ops).
   For both options we support OCSP stapling and CRL checks; rotation cadence is configurable (default 30 days).

2) Cross-region topology\- options:
   - Single private deployment per region (recommended for strict data residency / lowest latency). Traffic can fail over at DNS level; we provide stable region-specific endpoints and egress IPs.
   - Active-active fanout via a global routing layer (possible but requires coordination on cache/kv sync for session state).

3) Reranker latency\- target: 95th < 200ms is achievable if the reranker runs on the same private cluster and models are quantized for CPU/GPU mix. For the PoC we recommend co-locating embeddings + reranker in the private pool to avoid cross-network hops.

4) IP allowlisting / egress
   - We will provide per-region stable egress IP ranges for firewall rules. Example format: us-west-2 -> 34.210.0.0/16 (we will confirm exact ranges).
   - If you need a single static IP, we offer a NAT egress appliance option (extra).

5) SDK + structured output testing
   - Quick SDK init (sandbox):

     curl -X POST https://sandbox.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <SANDBOX_KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"summarize: clinical note", "structured_output": {"format":"json_schema_v1"}}'

   - For mTLS-enabled private endpoints (prod) use client certs:

     curl --cert client.pem --key client.key -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"..."}' https://private-us-west2.redwood.internal/v1/generate

6) Next steps for Thursday
   - Please confirm which mTLS model you prefer (customer-managed or Redwood-managed).
   - Share any existing egress IP allowlist constraints (firewall rules) you already have.
   - We will attach a short private-endpoint-specs.pdf with field names you’ll need for procurement/security review.

Attachments: private-endpoint-specs.pdf; redwood-onramp-checklist.xlsx

Thanks —
